Subject: On-site K8s roll: execution checklist and blockstore attach strategy

Sergio —

Attached is the execution checklist and a first pass blockstore attach strategy for the on-site deployment next month (see attachments: qualmhealth-onprem-checklist.xlsx, network-diagram-v1.png). I pulled together the cluster-level requirements we discussed in the intake call and a proposed node-pool split. High level asks before we lock the runbook: 

- Confirm rack-level constraints: whether nodes will be co-located with customer infra or in a dedicated rack (if dedicated, we need PDUs and labeling).
- Confirm storage frontend: do you plan to expose NVMe-oF fabric to the inference nodes, or will we consume SAN LUNs over iSCSI?
- Confirm LUN mapping policy and whether procurement will provide pre-created volumes (naming pattern) or we should script LUN creation via automation.

Key items in the checklist (summary):
1) Cluster topology: 1 control-plane (HA across 3 masters), 3 node pools (gp-infer, gp-io, gp-batch).
2) Storage: NVMe local for cache-ephemeral; shared blockstore for model artifacts served via CSI (we recommend RBD or multipath iSCSI depending on fabric).
3) Encryption: node-level LUKS + KMS/HSM integration for root and blockstore keys.
4) Networking: flat L2 for NVMe fabric; separate management VLAN; egress NAT per-tenant if requested.
5) Rollout: canary traffic shifting with 10% initial, PDBs and pod disruption budgets, automated rollback hooks.

Open items where we need your confirmation so we can finalise the runbook and assign tasks to field ops: rack constraints, storage fabric (NVMe-oF vs iSCSI), and whether your security team requires FIPS/HSM attestations in the runbook.

If helpful, Irene is copied and can expand on the NVMe attachment sequence. Can we lock a 60-minute kickoff for Nov 10th to sign off?

Thanks,

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Marissa —

Thanks for the checklist, looks thorough. A couple of clarifications from our infra side: 

- Our datacenter supports NVMe-oF on the new racks but a subset of older racks still present only iSCSI. For the initial phase we'd prefer NVMe for the inference fleet if you can consume it, otherwise fallback to iSCSI for specific hosts.
- For shared model artifacts we currently expect to provide RBD-backed volumes (Ceph) for smaller files and iSCSI LUNs for large frozen model blobs. Can your CSI driver support both RBD and iSCSI classes?
- KMS: we have an HSM appliance and use an internal KMS API. Can you document the KMS handshake steps so our security folks can validate?

Also curious on recommended reclaimPolicy for model volumes — we don't want models to be accidentally deleted during strikes, but we also want to automate snapshot/freeze workflows. Any recommended setting?

We can do Nov 10th for kickoff, but prefer 10:00–11:00 PT. I'll loop in procurement after the kickoff.

Sergio —

Quick technical notes from the field ops perspective. High-level answers to your points and explicit recommendations so we can capture them in the runbook: 

1) NVMe-oF vs iSCSI:
   - Recommendation: Use NVMe-oF for the gp-infer node pool (latency-sensitive). It reduces token-generation p99 by ~30–40% in our tests.
   - Fallback: For hosts on older racks, use multipath iSCSI with a CSI wrapper. We will detect the fabric during preflight and apply node labels (storage=nvme or storage=iscsi).

2) CSI support:
   - Our deployment uses the CSI pattern with two storage classes: sc-model-rbd (Ceph RBD, ReadWriteMany via object gateway for smaller artifacts) and sc-model-block (iSCSI/RBD-block, ReadWriteOnce with static provisioning for large model blobs). CSI snapshot and restore supported.

3) ReclaimPolicy:
   - For model artifacts: set reclaimPolicy=Retain + snapshots enabled. That prevents accidental deletion and allows automation to create lifecycle jobs to prune snapshots.
   - For ephemeral caches: reclaimPolicy=Delete on local ephemeral NVMe.

4) Encryption & KMS:
   - We will use node-level LUKS mapping for local devices and Ceph/RBD native encryption for backend. KMS integration: we need API endpoints and an HSM cert or client creds; we'll script key retrieval via an init-container on first attach. Please provide the HSM CA chain and an access test account (read-only key ops) for staging.

5) Node pools:
   - control-plane (3x m5-like, no GPUs).
   - gp-infer (GPU nodes, NVMe local cache, taint: inference=true:NoSchedule).
   - gp-io (IO-heavy nodes, attached block LUNs, high network connectivity).
   - Optional batch pool (cpu-only) for offline jobs.

6) Attachment model and daemon:
   - We'll deploy a small privileged daemonset that manages NVMe namespaces and handles attach/detach for local namespaces. For shared block devices, CSI will handle multipath attachment; we'll run a small operator to perform LUN discovery and idempotent mapping.

Irene

Looping in some deployment/ops considerations we should bake into the runbook: 

- Canary plan: start with a single gp-infer node and shift 10% traffic, monitor token latencies, memory pressure and KV cache hit rates for 48h before scaling to 30%.
- PDBs and draining: ensure PDBs are present for critical pods (model server, redis/kv) and use graceful drain with a 120s post-stop hook to flush KV cache to shared blockstore.
- Node taints/affinity: gp-infer nodes: taint inference=true:NoSchedule; use requiredDuringScheduling nodeAffinity for performance-critical pods.
- GPU isolation: use device-plugin with static topology hints so we avoid NUMA cross-socket allocation.
- Autoscaling policy: recommend KEDA for workload-based scaling of preprocessing jobs, and cluster-autoscaler for node pool scaling with custom metric mapping for GPU pods.
- Rollback: include automatic fallback to hosted Redwood Dedicated model (if network egress to Redwood allowed) for critical endpoints in case of site outage.

I'll add these lines to the runbook and tag tasks for preflight verification.

-Karthik
